author: l. l. phillips
title: Mark DeSaulnier addresses hate crimes and policy concerns across recent social media posts
text:
Mark DeSaulnier, U.S. Congressman representing California’s 10th district since 2015, recently addressed several key issues through a series of social media posts, including hate crimes against minority groups, immigration enforcement funding, and the importance of diversity in education.
On June 9, 2026, DeSaulnier highlighted findings from a recent nationwide poll: “A recent nationwide poll found that about one-quarter of Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander adults had personally experienced a hate crime or incident in the past year. I’m hosting a town hall on Wednesday, June 17th at 6:00 pm in Dublin with expert special” . This post comes as concerns about hate crimes continue to rise among these communities.
Later that same day, DeSaulnier criticized congressional spending priorities regarding immigration enforcement. He wrote, “What we DO need: A Republican majority that tackles the cost of living, reins in Trump’s overreach, and protects our communities. What we’re getting instead: $70 billion more for deadly and unconstitutional immigration enforcement. This isn’t just stupid – it’s reckless. And” on June 9, 2026.
On June 10, DeSaulnier turned his attention to local education and community values. Ahead of an @EdWorkforceDems hearing with San Francisco Unified School District Superintendent, he stated, “Here in the Bay Area, our greatness lies in our diversity and our tolerance. Ahead of today’s @EdWorkforceDems hearing with SFUSD Superintendent, I spoke with @ABC7newsbayarea about how we must all work together to support students, teachers, and families to make sure everyone in” .
Mark DeSaulnier has represented California’s 10th District since replacing George Miller in Congress in 2015. Before his time in Congress, he served on the Contra Costa County Board of Supervisors from 1994 to 2006; as a member of the California State Assembly from 2006 to 2008; and as a state senator from 2008 to 2015. Born in Lowell, Massachusetts in 1952 and currently residing in Concord at age 71, DeSaulnier graduated from College of the Holy Cross with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1974.
